rule: published artifacts stay byte-identical; corrections are appended
found_by: reading the other session's response() line by line after my own arm failed

entries.source_section_or_line: arm B, described as 'the trade price observable, as C-T52'
entries.old_statement: arm B measured R(1) on the trade price, came back NEGATIVE on all three (-0.0024 / -0.0134 / -0.4701), and was read as refuting the hypothesis that the observable explains the gap with C-T52
entries.corrected_statement: Arm B varied the observable but ALSO changed the alignment, so it was never the same estimand as theirs. Their response() computes R(1) = cum[0] = <eps_t (lp_t - lp_{t-1})>, the event's OWN move; my arm B computed <eps_t (p_{t+1} - p_t)>, the NEXT event's move. On a trade-price series those two differ by the whole bid-ask bounce, which is why one is positive and the other negative. The 2x2 in C-KULLIYAT-T52b separates them: trade price with the OWN alignment gives +0.0325 / +0.0806 / +0.5287, the same order and sign as C-T52. So the observable DOES largely explain the gap and the refutation was mine, not the hypothesis's. Also supersedes the note in C-KULLIYAT-T51's log block calling it a POPULATION difference: the populations are indeed disjoint (theirs 2026-07-23..27, mine 08-07..13) but that is a residual, not the mechanism.
